Reported past Mugling by 13:00

events.title: Devghat 4.76 m
events.detail: CHWRR calls this initial arrival; its chronology elsewhere gives 15:20. Sources conflict

events.title: Reported arrival at Devghat / Narayani
events.detail: CHWRR chronology; conflicts with its own 13:20 entry

events.title: Devghat peaks at 6.57 m (stage)
events.detail: Rating-curve estimates: ~5,850 m³/s; ~20 million m³ above baseline flow

events.title: International Charter activated
events.detail: Requested by DHM; satellite mapping begins

story.title: The collapse
story.text: Roughly 100 million m³ of rock and glacier ice (estimates vary by study) breaks off the Lirung massif at ~5,200 m and drops ~1.2 km into the valley. Seismometers record the collapse itself.

story.title: A debris flow forms
story.text: The falling mass becomes a debris flow, a fast slurry of mud, rock, ice and water, racing down the narrow Lende Khola gorge.

story.title: The border crossing is hit
story.text: CCTV shows it reaching the China–Nepal border about seven minutes after the collapse, at Gyirong Port, a busy crossing for traders and pilgrims.

story.title: Almost no warning downstream
story.text: The flow enters Nepal through Timure and Syabrubesi. River gauges stop transmitting one after another, so the timing here is bracketed rather than measured.

story.title: Warnings go out
story.text: At 09:15 emergency SMS alerts are dispatched along the river. The flow slows as the valley widens but remains destructive.

story.title: Down the Trishuli
story.text: Below Dhunche the river is the Trishuli. Around Betrawati hydropower projects, bridges and the riverside road are damaged or swept away.

story.title: A long, slower surge
story.text: Lower down the valley is wider and the flood wave travels more slowly, giving authorities time to warn towns further downstream.

story.title: Malekhu
story.text: At 11:26 the river at Malekhu crosses its warning level; by 11:43 it is above danger and the gauge and Phurke bridge are lost.

story.title: Past Mugling
story.text: By 13:00 the flood is reported past Mugling. Riverside residents as far as Devghat are told to move away from the banks.

story.title: Reaching the plains
story.text: Reports place arrival at Devghat and the Narayani around 15:20, though official records conflict. The river stage peaks at 6.57 m at 16:00, then falls.

story.title: What the map shows now
story.text: The shaded area is the satellite-mapped extent from the following days, revealed by estimated arrival time. Scrub the timeline or click a key event to revisit any moment.

after.title: Barrier lake warning (China MWR)
after.detail: Border lake ~2 million m³, more inflow expected

after.title: Two new lakes mapped
after.detail: ~12 ha and ~19 ha (UNOSAT polygons); CHWRR gives ~16 ha and ~18 ha

after.title: Lake 2 overflows
after.detail: Reported downstream rises; rescues briefly paused

lakes.name: Barrier lake 1
lakes.note: Lende–Lirung Khola confluence; reported overflowing from 28 Aug. Formed after the event

lakes.name: Barrier lake 2
lakes.note: Below the collapse area; reported overflow 29 Aug. Formed after the event

rows: ~103 million m³ (JMS); 99 ± 10 million m³ (JISRS); some reports cite ~132
M5.2 landslide signal (USGS); other agencies' magnitudes differ
14.2 km in ~350 s: a route-average rate (JMS), not a measured flow velocity
source.precursor: ICIMOD reports up to 40 cm of line-of-sight ground deformation at the source in Sentinel-1 radar between 7 Jul and 24 Aug; this is retrospective and does not imply the failure time was predictable.
source.rain: Satellite rainfall at the source grid cell was low before the failure (4.0 mm in 24 h, 20th percentile; 8.3 mm over 3 days), so heavy rain is not thought to be the main trigger. Local rainfall and initiation remain uncertain.
source.conflicts: Studies estimate geometry, volume, magnitude and speed differently; each figure is attributed to its source.
